minutes.headline: Town meeting passed the FY17 town budget unanimously; a water district study article drew a long, heated debate.
minutes.summary: The final town meeting in the old school auditorium passed the consent calendar, budget transfers, the capital plan, the FY17 operating budget, a salary plan, enterprise budgets and a new cable fund. An amendment to move school state aid into stabilization was withdrawn. Article 45, a study committee on making the Water District a town department, drew long debate and a counted vote on an amendment; the final result is not in the captions.

what_happened.line: Town Meeting passed the FY17 town budget (Article 15) unanimously, along with the capital plan and a salary plan cost-of-living article.
An amendment to move extra school state aid into the stabilization fund was withdrawn after assurances from the superintendent and school committee.
Town Meeting passed the solid waste, water and sewer enterprise budgets, a new inflow and infiltration stabilization fund, and a cable (PEG) fund, all unanimously.
On Article 45, the water district study committee, an amendment to change the committee makeup carried and an amendment to strike transition milestones failed on a counted vote.
The captions do not record the final result on Article 45 as amended, or the result on Article 22.

why_it_matters: The budget and enterprise votes set the town's spending for FY17, which draws on taxes, user fees and state aid, and the school line assumed extra state aid that had not yet arrived.

Article 45 bears on whether the Water District could become a town department, which could affect water service, rates and well owners outside the district, so its outcome is worth confirming from the official record.
